Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis (high likelihood): acute onset watery diarrhea 5-6 times/day, vomiting initially, mild fever at onset, no blood or abdominal pain, weakness, and dehydration due to poor intake  
- Past medical history of asthma noted; no medication changes or toxin exposures reported (medication side effects unlikely)  
- Family history relevant for bowel cancer, but presentation does not suggest colorectal cancer (low likelihood)  
- Inflammatory bowel disease flare less likely given absence of blood, pain, or chronic symptoms (moderate likelihood)  
- Other causes such as ischemic colitis, medication side effect, lactose intolerance less likely based on clinical presentation  
- No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx  

Management Plan  
- Advise adequate fluid intake and use of oral rehydration solutions (Dioralyte recommended)  
- Symptomatic treatment with paracetamol for fever and weakness  
- Advise rest and continued time off work until diarrhea-free for 24-48 hours  
- Follow-up arranged if symptoms persist beyond one week or worsen  
- No investigations immediately indicated; supportive care prioritized
